title: Critical Explosion
contents: p2e_start_trait_section
p2e_trait | common | Mechanic
p2e_end_trait_section
property | Prerequisites | Mine Exocortex

text | Your mines use bursts of shrapnel that shred through a creature, causing lasting harm. A creature that fails its saving throw against one of your mines takes an additional 1 persistent damage (or persistent damage equal to your Intelligence modifier on a critical failure). If the mine dealt physical damage, this is persistent bleed damage. Otherwise, the persistent damage is of the same type dealt by the mine.

title: Modify Pt. 1
contents: p2e_start_trait_section
p2e_trait | common | Mechanic
p2e_trait | common | Manipulate
p2e_end_trait_section
property | Requirements | You are holding or wearing your custom rig

text | Using your trusty custom rig, you quickly customize a piece of gear. Select one item in your possession or in the possession of a willing creature within your unarmed reach. If you select an item in your possession, you can Interact to draw or retrieve this item. Then, apply one of the mods you know to the item. The item remains modded until the end of your next turn. When you Modify an item, you can apply one of the following effects of your choice, called a mod, or any other mod you know. Some mods can only be applied to items of specific types or items with certain traits; these requirements are listed in parentheses.

title: Modify Pt. 2
contents: text | Big Boom (grenade or area weapon): You cram a big payload of explosives into a small package. Increase the item’s radius by 5 feet (if it’s a burst), its area by 5 feet (if it’s a cone), or its area by 10 feet (if it’s a line).

text | Bunker Buster (grenade or weapon): You amplify the destructive capabilities of an item. Whenever the item deals damage to an object, structure, vehicle, or create with Hardness, the target takes 5 additional damage. If the modded item has the razing trait, apply the additional damage from both this mod and the razing trait.
text | Incapacitant (grenade or weapon): You swap live ammunition for dummy rounds. The item gains the nonlethal trait.

title: Modify Pt. 3
contents: text | Magnetic Levitators (armor): You activate powerful magnets in your armor that propel the wearer off the ground. The wearer's land Speed gains hover, and the wearer gains a fly speed of 10 feet.
text | Long-Range Propulsors (grenade or ranged weapon): You increase the distance you can reliably shoot or throw the item. Increase the item’s range or range increment by 30 feet.
text | Troubleshoot (item): You quickly recalibrate a malfunctioning item. Reduce the value of the item’s glitching condition by 1.

title: Mine Pt. 1
contents: text | Your exocortex manages a network of mines. You can deploy these mines with the Deploy Mine action and activate them with the Detonate Mine action or reaction. Your mines are shielded and can’t detonate without your activation command. The DC to Disable your mines is equal to your class DC. You can collect all deployed and undetonated mines as a single action, storing them alongside your other prepared mines in your custom rig. During your daily preparations, you can create a number of mines up to 4 + your Intelligence modifier, which is also your maximum number of mines. This number increases by two at 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter. If you’re below this limit, you...

title: Mine Pt. 2
contents: text | ...can craft new mines using your custom rig. For every 10 minutes you spend in exploration mode, you create 2 mines; this doesn’t prevent you from participating in other exploration activities. You can store all your mines in your custom rig without increasing its Bulk. Though your mines are physical objects, they are destroyed if not used by the next time you make your daily preparations. They can’t be duplicated or preserved in any way. You can Modify one of your deployed mines at a range of 60 feet as if it were a grenade.

title: Deploy Mine
contents: p2e_start_trait_section
p2e_trait | common | Manipulate
p2e_trait | common | Mechanic
p2e_end_trait_section
property | Cost | 1 mine
text | You deploy a mine that flies to an unoccupied square of your choice within 60 feet and hovers in place.

text | Smart Mine (mine exocortex): You program your mines with rudimentary virtual intelligence, allowing them to avoid damaging specific targets. Select one target within 60 feet. That target is excluded from the area of all mines you detonate. At 5th level, you can instead select two targets.
text | Targeting Mine (mine exocortex): Your mines’ proximity sensors enable you to pinpoint creatures in range. Increase the mine’s damage by an amount equal to your Intelligence modifier.

title: Detonate Mine
contents: p2e_start_trait_section
p2e_trait | common | Concentrate
p2e_trait | common | Mechanic
p2e_end_trait_section
property | Requirements | A mine you deployed is within 150 feet

text | With a moment’s thought, you trigger the detonation of a mine you deployed within 150 feet, causing it to explode in a 10-foot burst. This mine deals your choice of either 2d6 fire damage or 2d6 piercing damage. Creatures in the area must attempt a basic Reflex save against your class DC.
text | You can Detonate Mine as a reaction, with the following trigger.
text | Trigger A creature enters or leaves a square within the 10 feet of a mine you have deployed. If your mine has a larger radius, increase this distance to that amount.
text | At 3rd level and every 2 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d6. At 10th level, the burst radius increases to 15 feet, and at 15th level, the burst radius increases to 20 ft

title: Custom Rig
contents: text | You begin with a specialized toolkit called a custom rig. Your custom rig has 1 Bulk and counts as both a commercial toolkit and any one of the following toolkits: a commercial hacking toolkit, <u> a commercial infiltrator's toolkit</u>, or a commercial maker's toolkit. You can use your custom rig with one hand if you're wearing it or two hands if you're holding it. Whenever you purchase one of the listed toolkits, you can spend 10 minutes integrating that toolkit into your custom rig without increasing its Bulk. Your custom rig and any integrated toolkits can't be sold or used by another creature. If your custom rig is lost or destroyed, you can spend 1 hour building a new one. Your previous custom rig stops functioning, and your new custom rig doesn't have the properties of any previously integrated toolkits.

title: Arrest a Fall
contents: property | Requirements | You have a fly Speed.
property | Trigger | You fall.
text | You attempt your choice of an Acrobatics check or Reflex save to slow your fall. The DC is typically 15, but it might be higher due to air turbulence or other circumstances.
text | Success You take no damage from the fall.

text | Infosphere archivists have lived by the credo that information wants to be free, and you know where to find it. You Access Infosphere. On a critical failure, in addition to the usual effects, your comm unit becomes glitching 5.

title: Programmer
contents: p2e_start_trait_section
p2e_trait | common | General
p2e_trait | common | Skill
p2e_end_trait_section
property | Prerequisites | Trained in Computers

text | You can write computer programs. You can Earn Income using Computers, spending your time programming apps for clients. You can also Craft items with the virtual trait. You can use Programmer to Craft tech items that don't have the virtual trait, but you can only cover up to a quarter of the item's cost in raw materials; the remaining Crafting has to be completed by someone using the Crafting skill.

title: Starship Combat
contents: text | Mechanics are at home helming the generator, where they can Reposition Shield using Crafting or benefit from the mechanic generator module upgrade, but they can push practically any battle station they helm past its limit depending on the ship's equipment. The mechanic generator module allows a mechanic to add unique mods to a starship that can turn the tide of battle. The pet drone shell, mine deployment shell, and gunnery turret mount allow mechanics in starship combat to deploy their drones, mines, and turrets, respectively. Mechanics who invest in their mine exocortex might also want to helm a drone console with a pryotechnics drone. Mechanics can Modify any gunnery weapon.

title: Access Infosphere
contents: p2e_start_trait_section
p2e_trait | common | Exploration
p2e_trait | common | Concentrate
p2e_trait | common | Secret
p2e_end_trait_section
property | Requirements | You are using a device with Infosphere access.
property | Skill | Computers

text | You attempt to access a local network, known as an infosphere, to come up with information on a topic. This typically takes 10 minutes of research to find information, with results like Recalling Knowledge on a topic. Larger investigations or topics could require several hours, while single-word answers of information common to that settlement's infosphere may only take a minute, based on the GM's discretion. Significant and longer investigations should use the research subsystem (GM Core). The GM determines the DC based on the topic you're researching. This can be further influenced by the quality of the local infosphere and what information it might possess on the topic, and how well organized it is.
text | Critical Success You find the information you were searching for. If this was used on a topic you could have used Recall Knowledge on, you instead find this information in 1 minute.
text | Success You find the information you were looking for.

text | Critical Failure You find misleading information thanks to incorrect data or online pranksters. The GM provides you false information on your topic of investigation (or decides to give you no information, as on a failure).

title: Earn Income
contents: p2e_start_trait_section
p2e_trait | common | Downtime
p2e_end_trait_section

text | You use one of your skills to make money during downtime. The GM assigns a task level representing the most lucrative job available. You can search for lower-level tasks, with the GM determining whether you find any. Sometimes you can attempt to find better work than the initial offerings, though this takes time and requires using the Diplomacy skill to Gather Information, doing some research, or socializing. When you take on a job, the GM secretly sets the DC of your skill check. After your first day of work, you roll to determine your earnings. You gain an amount of income based on your result, the task's level, and your proficiency rank (as listed on the Income Earned table). You can continue working at the task on subsequent days without needing to roll again. For each day you spend after the first, you earn the same amount as the first day, up until the task's completion. The GM determines how long you can work at the task. Most tasks last a week or two, though some can take months or even years.
text | Critical Success You do outstanding work. Gain the amount of currency listed for the task level + 1 and your proficiency rank.
text | Success You do competent work. Gain the amount of currency listed for the task level and your proficiency rank

text | Failure You do shoddy work and get paid the bare minimum for your time. Gain the amount of currency listed in the failure column for the task level. The GM will likely reduce how long you can continue at the task.

text | Critical Failure You earn nothing for your work and are fired immediately. You can't continue at the task. Your reputation suffers, potentially making it difficult for you to find rewarding jobs in that community in the future.
